subject: Request: Temporary uptime & latency remedy waiver + commercial concession
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@bluehaven.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 15:22 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime/latency remedy waiver + commercial ask

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles on short sequences. We are nearing procurement signoff but have two gating items coming from legal and ops: a) Bluehaven requires that for the pilot we get an uptime floor set at 99.5% for the dedicated pool or a commensurate service credit cap, and b) because of data residency routing work, we need a temporary latency remedy allowance that tolerates occasional 150-200ms bursts above our agreed P95 for up to three weeks during our import window.

Procurement is pushing for a short-term commercial concession to compensate for the operational lift: a 12% one-time platform credit against the first three months of committed spend if we can get the waiver and a 30-day onboarding SLA commitment from Redwood.

I've attached our security questionnaire and a draft amendment to the SLA to show the language legal is pushing. Can Redwood provide an exec-level response (deal desk + revenue approval) to confirm whether you can:
- Accept a temporary latency remedy carveout limited to the import window (dates supplied once we finalize schedule)
- Cap service credits to either a fixed $$ amount or at most a single-month credit, rather than the full rolling remedy proposed in your standard SLA
- Offer the one-time 12% credit as described if the waiver is granted

We'd like an answer by Monday to keep the procurement timeline. Happy to hop on a call if that's easier.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement
Bluehaven Therapeutics
Attachments: Bluehaven_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, SLA_Amendment_Bluehaven_v1.1.docx
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@bluehaven.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 09:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime/latency remedy waiver + commercial ask

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the docs.

I’ve looped in Marissa from commercial and Jonas from deal desk to assess whether we can approve a temporary, scoped remedy carveout and the credit request. High level from my side: we are supportive of making the pilot low-friction, but we need to preserve our remedy exposure in a way that doesn’t materially increase risk for other customers.

Next steps we’ll take today:
- Marissa: commercial recommendation and whether 12% credit fits within our pricing guardrails.
- Jonas: deal desk analysis on operational risk and proposed alternative remedy language (fixed cap vs. single-month credit).
- I’ll confirm whether onboarding SLA commitments can be tightened to 30 days for pilot customers in our Dedicated offering.

If possible, Maria — can you confirm the expected import window dates (rough range) and an estimate of peak QPS during that time? That will help us size the risk.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 11:42 -0700
Subject: Bluehaven: commercial + authorization request (DEAL-2026-0098) — recommendation included

Team — summarizing the ask from Bluehaven (see attached Deal_Summary_DEAL-2026-0098.xlsx):
- Temporary latency remedy allowance during a 3-week import window (expected mid-May to early June) tolerating P95 spikes up to +200ms.
- Request to cap service credits to either a fixed $20k cap or to at most a single month of committed spend instead of our standard rolling remedy formula.
- One-time commercial credit of 12% applied to first three months of committed spend.

Recommendation (commercial):
- Approve the temporary latency carveout for the stated import window with two controls: 1) it is time-boxed (max 21 consecutive days) and 2) it only applies to requests tagged with the Bluehaven import prefix (no global KV cache invalidation).
- Approve service-credit cap at $20k for the pilot period (this provides a bounded exposure).
- Offer a one-time 8% platform credit instead of 12% (12% exceeds our new ACV concession thresholds). Require a short-term clause: if import window extends beyond 3 weeks or we observe >3 outage incidents during the window attributable to Redwood, the credit drops to 0% and standard remedies reapply.

Financial note (Priyom): please confirm whether 8% is within acceptable margin impact for an initial 6-month commit. If not, provide upper/lower bounds.

Approval requested: Exec signoff for the adjusted credit (8%) and the $20k cap. If approved, Deal Desk will produce the SLA amendment language and updated commercial terms for signature.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@bluehaven.com>
Date: Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 08:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Bluehaven: commercial + authorization request (DEAL-2026-0098) — deal desk analysis

Folks — quick operational readout and proposed redline language.

Operational assessment:
- Bluehaven’s import QPS estimate: ~150 r/s sustained for 48–72 hours with short bursts to 400 r/s. With Dedicated pool sizing we proposed, risk is moderate but manageable with temporary burst capacity. The main exposure is KV cache churn and cold-start amplification during high-concurrency ingestion which could increase tail latency.

Proposed remedy language (for SLA amendment draft):
"For a defined Pilot Import Window (not to exceed 21 calendar days and to be scheduled no later than 90 days from execution), Redwood will allow an operational latency tolerance for P95 up to +200ms relative to the committed baseline for requests tagged with the Bluehaven-import prefix. This tolerance does not apply to production traffic outside the import tag. Redwood's aggregate service credit exposure for incidents occurring within the Pilot Import Window will be capped at $20,000. Should the Pilot Import Window extend beyond 21 days or produce more than three qualifying incidents attributable to Redwood, the standard SLA remedies will supersede this amendment."

Notes:
- The tag-based approach avoids global impact.
- We should include a requirement for Bluehaven to stagger uploads and accept throttling guidance during the import window.

I will prep the SLA_Amendment_Bluehaven_v1.1.docx with the redline and return a clean copy for signature if we get exec authorization on the 8% credit and the $20k cap.

Jonas
Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Bluehaven: commercial + authorization request (DEAL-2026-0098) — exec decision

Thanks for the clear summary. I’m comfortable approving the deal desk recommendation with the following gates:
1) Final signoff contingent on Priyom confirming cost impact of an 8% one-time credit on first three months by EOD Monday. If finance flags material margin erosion, we revert to 5% max.
2) SLA amendment must include the tag-based limitation and the $20k hard cap verbatim; no language that weakens our ability to return to standard remedies outside the pilot.
3) Bluehaven must agree to a staging plan (upload schedule) and a post-import health check with Redwood within seven days of completion.

Camila — you have exec-level approval contingent on Priyom’s finance confirmation. Please capture the conditions in the amendment and send back to Maria for countersignature.

—Avery
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
